decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [BDLK11-MMA-V1-ZZ-DR-A-21102(P2), BDLK11-MMA-V1-ZZ-DR-A-21103 (P2), BDLK11-MMA-V1-ZZ-DR-A-21106(P2), BDLK11-MMA-V1-ZZ-DR-A-21105 (P1), BDLK11-MMA-V1-ZZ-DR-A-21104 (P1), Transport Statement ( dtd 15/08/2025, by Mayer Brown), Travel Plan,  Biodiversity Technical Note, Biodiversity Metric sheet, Technical sheet on foundations, Technical sheet on Chiller, Plant Sound Assessment, Fire statement, application form- 28/08/2025; Operation and Maintenance Manual, Response to Pre-Commencement Condition on Contamination, 8230627-4502 Underground utility sheet mapping- Received 15/10/2025; Transport Addendum (by Mayer Brown)- Received 20/10/2025; Construction Logistics Plan (dtd 23/10/2025, by Roxi Fullbrook Mace PM) � Received 23/10/2025].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.

Condition : 4 - The proposal must be implemented as per the approved Construction Logistics Plan. HGV deliveries to the site shall take place between between 9.30am-3.00pm. 
Reason- In the interest of highway safety and neighbouring amenities.

Condition : 5 - Notwithstanding the submitted details and prior to occupation, full details (including manufacturer' s specifications) of all cycle stands for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The provisions must accord with the West London Cycle Parking Guidance. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before any part of the development is first occupied and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction. 
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 6 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include;
(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat,
(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development,
(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and
(f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years.
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.

Condition : 7 - Habitat management plan. 

Notwithstanding the submitted details, no above ground works, excluding demolition, remediation and groundworks, shall take place until a habitat management plan in accordance with any approved Biodiversity Gain Plan must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The habitat management plan shall include:
a)	Prescription for management actions.
b)	Preparation of the work schedule (including an annual work Plan for over 30-year period and who will carry out the jobs mentioned in the management plans).
c)	Details of the body or organisation responsible for implementation of the plan.
d)	Time frame for reviewing the plan.
e)	Details of the management plans and its communication to the occupiers of the development.
Reason: In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Informative:
This condition shall apply if the Biodiversity Gain Plan identifies the delivery of on-site and/or off-site habitats to meet the minimum Biodiversity Net Gain requirement.

Condition : 8 - Contamination- Additional/unexpected contamination found during development. 
During the development:
Site staff shall receive appropriate training regarding site's history and any previous remediation measures. A visual inspection shall be undertaken prior to any groundworks to identify the presence of any landfill remediation measures. The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any previous remediation measures are damaged or any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues.  A remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination.  
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety. 
To ensure that the existing landfill containment, gas venting and leachate control systems are not compromised by the proposed works, thereby safeguarding the environment and public health.
Supporting notes:
(i) Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii) In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii) The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hou

Condition : 9 - Contamination - Verification Report. 
Prior to the development is first brought into use:
If unexpected contamination is encountered, a verification report prepared by a suitably qualified environmental engineer shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority following completion of all groundworks and prior to occupation of the development. The report shall confirm that all approved protection measures have been implemented as agreed and that the existing landfill containment systems remain intact, functional and undisturbed.
Reason: 
To verify that the approved protection measures have been effectively implemented and that the integrity of the landfill containment and gas/leachate management systems has been maintained.
Supporting notes:
(i) The verification (closure) report shall provide evidence that all approved protection measures have been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. 
(ii) This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality and human health.
(iii) The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 10 - a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which this permission refers, shall be 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, at all times that the plant operate. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises, and in accordance to the latest British Standard 4142. An alternative position for assessment/measurement may be used to allow ease of access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria are achieved. 

b) The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter.   

c) Following installation of any mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which the application refers, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the local planning authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again.  This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the required standard.  Once achieved, the plant shall be maintained permanently ther

Condition : 11 - Emergency Generators.
Prior to use, all details of the emergency generator shall be submitted to and approved by the local authority to confirm that sound emitted by standby or emergency generators during power outages or testing does not exceed the lowest daytime ambient noise level LAeq(15min) as measured or calculated according to BS4142:2014. For the purpose of testing, testing is permitted for up to 1 hour per month between 09.00 and 17.00 Monday to Friday only and not on public holidays.
Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the amenities of occupiers of neighbouring properties.
